title: Preserve diagnostic bytes in unittest benchmark receipt comparisons
body:
The integrated PR921 benchmark can report identical receipts after substantive stderr changes: timing-shaped failure text (`in 1.000s` → `in 2.000s`) is erased by its unanchored regex, and distinct bytes `ff`/`fe` collide under replacement decoding. Both collisions reproduce with real unittest captures; bounded fault injection makes the unchanged benchmark report PASS.

Add `research/unittest-receipt-comparison` with a byte-preserving comparator and an opt-in adapter for the exact pinned benchmark. Only the elapsed value in the final standard unittest trailer may differ. Explicit raw/summary tags and a prefix length prevent normalization-marker collisions. The predecessor's commands, module inventory, raw stdout hashes, exit-code checks and mismatch rejection remain intact.

Validation on Windows 11 / CPython 3.12.10:

- 20 focused tests pass through the registered replay in normal and optimized Python, including real captures and end-to-end benchmark controls.
- Source pins, package metadata, affected-package selection and `git diff --check` pass.
- All 42 onboarding tests pass with `PYTHONUTF8=1`; workspace TEMP/TMP was used for sandbox-compatible fixtures.

The entire repository benchmark and selected mathematical replay were not run. No performance, new kappa, historical-run defect or full-suite equivalence claim. Frozen inputs and the selected record are unchanged.

Base main: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. Portable-replay, priority revision 3; selector nonce `d478b42a7ca6903045649ed7bd64bc93`. TASK/SOURCES/RESULT/VALIDATION/VERIFY record scope, exact provenance, controls, remaining obligations and replay commands. Final overlap covered 573 open PRs and 542 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings; no matching external scope found, which is not proof of novelty. [Coordination claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1916).

Credit Aaron Wang/navinor (PR921, reviewed head `c1ee2fbfdc5700a1ba0251e7727ee8ae0cb4782f`) and Douglas Colkitt's batch932 acceptance hardening. Related PR1852 addresses child assertions separately. Prepared by Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human review; Apache-2.0.
